free_tier.stated: unlimited storage advertised; 5 GB/file anonymous, 20 GB/file with a free account

retention.stated: 5 GB/file anonymous (7 days after last download), 20 GB/file free account (30 days after last download)

egress.terms: unmetered, but free downloads carry an explicit human-verification step

tooling: documented REST API; GET /api/files?url={fileUrl} for status. Upload-via-API docs are Premium-only ('Docs for the upload steps are Premium only').
chaining: free accounts are free and email-only; 20 GB/file x N accounts. Storage advertised as unlimited per account.
limits_note: 5 GB/file anonymous (7 days after last download), 20 GB/file free account (30 days after last download). Premium removes the human check and the size limit; premium is granted only to partner sites with 200k+ visits/month, not sold.
reliability_note: Its own FAQ says premium 'removes the ads and the "verify you are human" check on downloads' — i.e. free downloads require human verification by design. That alone disqualifies it for automated fetch. It also ships a download manager because 'browser downloads stall on big files'.

evidence.proved: 'Docs for the upload steps are Premium only'

notes: unlimited storage advertised; 5 GB/file anonymous, 20 GB/file with a free account

extras.probe_reported: POST https://akirabox.com/upload -> 404 'Server action not found.' (Next.js server action, needs browser-issued action id). Upload path NOT scriptable from curl.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
